title: Security guards between sites

blocks.text: A security company rosters guards over a few nights. Each night every guard is at exactly one **place**: a site, or home (off duty). Places are numbered `0, 1, ..., n - 1`, and the last one, `n - 1`, is home. `need[d]` maps a site to the number of guards it needs on night `d`; a site missing from `need[d]` needs none that night, and home takes any number. Moving a guard from place `p` on one night to place `q` the next costs `cost[p][q]` (and `cost[p][p] = 0`), and some moves are not allowed at all: a guard coming off a night at the port cannot be at the airport the next night, for example.

Write `plan_nights(guards, need, cost, forbidden)` in `guards.py`. `forbidden` lists the not-allowed `(p, q)` moves. Return `(total, at)`, where `at[(guard, d)]` is the guard's place on night `d`, chosen so that the total cost of all moves is as small as possible. Every instance in the tests has a plan.

The model, with $`G`$ the guards, nights $`d = 0, \dots, N - 1`$, places $`0, \dots, n-1`$, demand $`m_{d,p}`$ for each site $`p < n - 1`$, the cost table $`T`$ flattened row by row ($`\tau_{n p + q} = T_{p,q}`$) and the forbidden moves $`F`$:

The (move cost) rows are element constraints, the (forbidden) rows forbidden-assignment constraints. Read the flattening carefully: which index is the row? The tests check the roster you return and its total, so any optimal roster passes. Some tests pass an empty `forbidden` list, which forbids nothing; the reference adds the forbidden-assignment rows only when the list is not empty, and you may do the same. Return the total as an `int`, with `round(solver.objective_value)`. About twenty-five lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from ortools.sat.python import cp_model


def plan_nights(guards: list[str], need: list[dict[int, int]], cost: list[list[int]],
                forbidden: list[tuple[int, int]]) -> tuple[int, dict[tuple[str, int], int]]:
    """(total move cost, (guard, night) -> place) of the cheapest roster."""
    # TODO: one Boolean per guard, night and place, the place number, the need rows, the forbidden
    # moves and each move's cost read from the flattened table. Placeholders below.
    return -1, {(g, d): -1 for g in guards for d in range(len(need))}


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(plan_nights(["ana", "ben"], [{0: 1, 1: 1}, {0: 1}, {1: 2}],
                      [[0, 3, 1], [3, 0, 1], [1, 1, 0]], [(0, 1)]))

cases.says: when every site needs the same guards every night, nobody moves and the cost is 0
every guard gets one place each night, and each site gets the guards it needs
a move from place p to place q costs entry [p][q] of the table, which can differ from [q][p]
no guard makes a forbidden move from one night to the next

origin.section: Forbidden Pairs and a Flattened Element Price a Crew's Moves

concepts: forbidden assignments remove listed pairs, and a two-dimensional table is read by element at n times the row plus the column
a roster over a few fixed slots is one Boolean per person and slot, with exactly-one, at-most-one and count rows
